summary: This is the thermostat's display method rewritten to hand back a status line as a String instead of printing it, which makes the value easy to check in a test.

lines.text: The listing shows only the part of Thermostat that changed; the class itself is the same one built earlier in the chapter.
This comment stands in for the fields, constructor, and getStatus method already written, so the page can focus on the one method being modified.
Declaring the return type as String instead of void means the method now produces a value the caller can capture, compare, or assert on.
The label and the current status are joined into a single string and returned, leaving the decision about where to display it to whoever calls the method.
